neighbourhoods.name: Swadlincote

housing: South Derbyshire is one of the fastest-growing districts in the East Midlands, with large new-build estates around Swadlincote, Hilton and the southern edge of Derby. Older homes include Victorian terraces in Swadlincote and Woodville from the area's clay, pottery and coal industries, and Georgian brick houses in Melbourne and Repton. Most households own their home and private renting is below average. The National Forest covers much of the south of the district.
checkinTips: New-build estates around Swadlincote, Hilton and Stenson Fields: photograph snagging items, sealant, paintwork and the garden, and note who maintains shared areas.
Victorian terraces in Swadlincote and Woodville: record the back yard, rear gate, gutters and any cracks or damp, as some homes stand on old mining land.
Georgian cottages in Melbourne and Repton: photograph sash windows, chimney breasts and any damp on solid walls.
Homes near the River Trent: check ground floors, gardens and outbuildings for signs of past flooding.
Village homes off the gas grid: photograph the oil tank and gauge level or LPG tank, and any wood burner.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems can contact South Derbyshire District Council's Environmental Health team, which can inspect privately rented homes and take action against landlords.
